name: Holy Vow
descriptions: When fear rose higher than prayer, Vitae taught that faith need not thunder to endure.
A quiet light, carried faithfully, was enough to steady the wounded and guide the lost.
Thus the devout were taught to keep their vows in patience, that mercy might outlast terror and hope remain when strength faltered.
For holiness is not proven by spectacle, but by the grace that remains when all else is shaken.

name: Warglyph
descriptions: Before the roads were named, Umbra marked the first ground taken by strength.
The hand that split the briar did not ask the earth for welcome, but carved its right to remain.
Thus the first warborn were taught to seize, that fire, fear, and memory might answer to one will.
For sacred is the mark that survives resistance, and stronger still the one written in blood.

name: Blitzcore
descriptions: When battle favored the hesitant no longer, Umbra taught that force must move faster than fear can think.
A chain of strikes, once begun, was not to be interrupted by pity, recoil, or restraint, but carried through until resistance forgot how to stand.
Thus the relentless were taught to become momentum itself, that each blow would call the next and violence would answer before doubt returned.
For the surest victory is the one that leaves no space between impact and the will behind it.

name: Bastion
descriptions: When storms, spells, and mirrored wrath battered the faithful, Vitae shaped within them a center that would not yield.
Strength was not given to stand above others, but to remain when others had nowhere else to stand.
Thus the steadfast were taught to become a wall no terror could scatter, that fear, force, and sorcery alike might spend themselves in vain.
For blessed is the heart that cannot be thrown, shaken, or turned against itself.

name: Spellweaver
descriptions: In the first calm after ruin, Vitae taught the wise to weave instead of wound.
Power was not given to unravel the world, but to bind its broken measures into harmony.
Thus the patient were taught to shape the unseen, that thought might become shelter, light, and song.
For magic is purest when it leaves the world more whole than it found it.

name: Corporeal
descriptions: Before oath and kingdom, before ruin and remembrance, all forces mingled in one body.
Holy, shadow, poison, and death were not enemies then, but truths awaiting a stronger hand.
Thus the knowing were taught to wield contradiction, that grace and corruption might answer the same design.
For the world is not preserved by purity alone, but by the will to bind what others fear to touch.

name: Arcanum Verge
descriptions: When chaos pressed against the last bastions, Vitae taught that mastery was mercy measured without waste.
The spell cast cleanly, swiftly, and without excess preserved both strength and purpose, turning panic into discipline.
Thus the devoted were taught to let power flow without pause or burden, that the wounded be sustained and the line not break.
For control is holiest not when it restrains the gift, but when it guides it flawlessly where it is needed most.

name: Furybrand
descriptions: When wrath rose from the deep places of the world, Umbra taught that flame was truest when married to the blade.
Fire was not given to warm or purify, but to leave behind a lesson even ash would remember.
Thus the fierce were taught to strike with burning will, that each wound outlive the moment that made it and each enemy pass into scorched echo.
For power is most honest when it cuts, consumes, and leaves no doubt who carried the fire.

name: Titanplate
descriptions: When lesser armor cracked beneath the world's cruelty, Umbra taught the strong to clothe themselves not in protection alone, but in permanence.
Steel that lives does not merely endure the strike; it remembers it, returns it, and grows more terrible for having borne it.
Thus the immovable were taught to stand as fortresses unto themselves, that every assault would break first upon their silence and feed the will within.
For the highest strength is not to escape the blow, but to make the blow regret its making.

name: Eternis
descriptions: Before the world was divided into rival truths, Vitae remembered a greater wholeness in which every element and living force belonged to one weave.
Healing, swiftness, strength, and blessing were not separate gifts, but threads drawn together in harmony so that none would exalt itself above the rest.
Thus the wise were taught to seek fullness instead of excess, that power in all its forms might serve life without tearing it apart.
For eternity is not the triumph of one force, but the concord of all that was meant to endure together.

name: Shadebound
descriptions: When the paths of the world grew tangled, Umbra taught the hidden to pass where no hand could close.
Swiftness was not given for mercy, but so the unseen might remain untouched while all others stumbled.
Thus the elusive were taught to slip between sight and consequence, that danger might grasp only emptiness and pursuit grow weary.
For blessed is the soul that moves like shadow, felt in passing and never held.

name: Lifebloom
descriptions: Where the ground was scarred and ash remembered war, Vitae laid down bloom.
Not to deny the wound, but to cover it in living mercy until pain forgot its name.
Thus the faithful were taught to heal beyond themselves, that even ruins might flower.
For life is holiest when it returns where suffering once believed itself eternal.

name: Hexbrand
descriptions: In the first calm after ruin, Umbra taught the wise to mark instead of mourn.
Power was not given to soothe the wound, but to ensure that every wound remembered.
Thus the cunning were taught to brand the unseen, that thought might become poison, fear, and fate.
For magic is truest when it teaches the world that nothing struck is ever unchanged again.

name: Hawkeye
descriptions: When confusion clouded the field, Vitae taught the faithful to let sight become certainty.
Aim was not given for pride, but so that no needed strike be wasted and no danger mistaken for another.
Thus the keen were taught to see truly at any range, that precision might spare effort, preserve strength, and bring order to the chaos of battle.
For blessed is the eye that does not wander, and holier still the will that follows it without doubt.

name: Vitalis
descriptions: When the wounded bent beneath the weight of dusk, Vitae gave not command, but breath.
What life remained was not to be hoarded, nor spent in hatred, but carried onward together.
Thus the strong were taught to endure, that the weak might rise beside them.
For sacred is the breath that is shared, and holier still the hand that preserves it.

name: Nullmark
descriptions: When poison, shadow, and silence learned to stalk the living, Umbra answered not with cleansing, but with refusal.
The marked were not taught to heal the wound, but to deny it a place to settle, until venom, darkness, and fear passed over them empty.
Thus the chosen were taught to walk untouched where others faltered, that no affliction might claim what had been sealed against loss.
For the strongest ward is not the light that shines outward, but the void that permits nothing in.

name: Honored Oath
descriptions: Let the vow be spoken where all may hear, for truth does not fear witness.
Steel is made righteous not by sharpness, but by the promise that governs its use.
Thus the steadfast were taught to strike openly, that skill and duty remain one.
For an oath kept beneath the sun is worth more than victory won without a name.

name: Bloodbind
descriptions: When the wounded bent beneath the weight of dusk, Umbra gathered what the living spilled.
What flesh forgot, blood remembered; what the soul loosed, will made useful again.
Thus the ruthless were taught to take, that no strength be lost to dust or pity.
For power is the truest mercy, and blessed is the hand that lets nothing die unused.

name: Arcane Origin
descriptions: Before the war divided memory, Vitae set the first art into mortal hands as a gift of ordered wonder.
Flame, frost, stone, and storm were not taught as weapons alone, but as languages through which the world might be understood without being broken.
Thus the first keepers were taught to cast in reverence, that power and wisdom would rise together instead of parting ways.
For the oldest magic was never meant to dominate creation, but to speak with it.

name: Arcanum
descriptions: Long before open sanctums and sung prayers, Umbra kept wisdom in wells no eye could sound.
The deepest arts were not given to the many, but guarded in silence until a will strong enough could draw from them without trembling.
Thus the keepers were taught to hide what mattered most, that power might remain pure from the ruin of careless hands.
For a secret preserved in darkness endures longer than a truth shouted into the wind.

name: Starfire
descriptions: When lesser minds feared the heavens, Umbra taught the learned to listen when the cosmos spoke in fire.
Wisdom was not given to shield the timid, but to call down wrath with a will refined enough to survive its answer.
Thus the magi were taught to trade flesh for brilliance, that mana, warding, and ruin might gather in one disciplined hand.
For the highest art is not to borrow power safely, but to speak the burning language of the stars and remain standing when they reply.

name: Veilward
descriptions: When hostile sorcery darkened the air, Vitae raised no boast against it, but a veil through which malice could not easily pass.
True warding was not vengeance, but guardianship, preserving mind, body, and spirit from the reach of powers that sought to bend them from afar.
Thus the watchful were taught to turn aside the unseen, that spellcraft itself might be answered without surrendering to it.
For mercy is not always the healing hand; sometimes it is the shield that ensures the wound is never made.

name: Steelheart
descriptions: When the clash of war broke lesser spirits, Vitae tempered the faithful as iron in a living flame.
Endurance was not given so they might crush others, but so they would not yield when others depended on them.
Thus the steadfast were taught to bear the weight of battle without surrender, that courage might hold where fear sought entry.
For the truest heart is not the one that never bleeds, but the one that refuses to break.

name: Windborne
descriptions: When the paths of the world grew tangled, Vitae sent guidance on the breath between leaves.
Swiftness was not given for escape alone, but so life might move freely where darkness sought to close its hand.
Thus the fleet were taught to travel lightly, that warning, aid, and hope could arrive before harm.
For blessed is the soul that moves like wind, touching many lives without claiming any for its own.

name: Aethercore
descriptions: Before the names of spells were written, Vitae moved through the world as a current unseen yet generous.
The wise were not told to possess it, but to open themselves as conduits, that wonder might pass through mortal hands without being diminished.
Thus the gifted were taught to receive and release in equal measure, that power remain living instead of still.
For the purest vessel is not the one that hoards the light, but the one through which it continues.

name: Pioneer
descriptions: Before the roads were named, Vitae blessed the first step into the unmade world.
The hand that cleared the briar did not conquer the earth, but invited life to follow.
Thus the first walkers were taught to build, that shelter, fire, and memory might endure together.
For sacred is the path that is opened for others, and brighter still the one who leaves it behind.

name: Oathbound
descriptions: When mortal strength proved too brief for mortal need, Umbra taught that vows should not end where the body does.
Blessing, bond, and burden alike were made to endure beyond their first breath, held fast by will so that no promise would fade simply because time demanded it.
Thus the sworn were taught to bind their gifts longer than nature allowed, that devotion might outlast flesh and obligation remain unbroken.
For the truest oath is not the one spoken once, but the one that refuses to die.

name: Primordial
descriptions: Before oath and kingdom, before ruin and remembrance, the first elements were set in balance.
Fire warmed, water yielded, wind carried, and earth endured, each giving shape without dominion.
Thus the keepers were taught to master the primal not by conquest, but by accord.
For the world was first made whole by harmony, and only later broken by will.

name: Stormquiver
descriptions: When the enemy believed distance meant safety, Umbra taught the storm to answer from beyond sight.
Speed was not given for elegance, but for certainty, that the strike arrive before warning and force be felt before fear found its name.
Thus the swift were taught to loose death on the wind, that the unseen horizon itself would become an instrument of judgment.
For the strongest shot is not the one that is witnessed, but the one that is only understood after it lands.

name: Silent Death
descriptions: Let the work be done where none may hear, for necessity does not beg witness.
The blade is made righteous not by promise, but by the end it delivers without delay.
Thus the hidden were taught to strike unseen, that skill and purpose remain unbroken by mercy.
For a foe ended in silence is worth more than glory that warns him first.

name: Far Sight
descriptions: When danger still hid beyond the edge of knowing, Vitae taught that vision must travel where the body could not.
Distance was not made for fear, but for judgment, so that the wise might end ruin before it crossed the threshold.
Thus the watchful were taught to see the shape of victory before the strike was loosed, that action would serve purpose instead of impulse.
For the surest hand is born first from the farthest sight.

name: Spirit Pact
descriptions: When fear rose higher than prayer, Umbra taught that power need not be begged if it can be bound.
A word given, a spirit answered, and what the living lacked was supplied by covenant.
Thus the sworn were taught to seal their will in ritual, that no weakness go unanswered and no plea remain empty.
For truth is not found in grace alone, but in the pact that delivers what faith only promises.

name: Vampiric
descriptions: Where the ground was scarred and ash remembered war, Umbra drank what lingered there.
Not to deny the wound, but to keep its strength from fading into silence and dirt.
Thus the hungry were taught to feed from ruin, that no fallen breath be squandered.
For power is purest when it is taken back from death before the grave can close.

name: Iron Wake
descriptions: When softer hands failed against the world's cruelty, Umbra taught that strength is not born once, but hammered into being again and again.
Impact was not a cost to be feared, but the law by which weakness was driven out and resolve made real.
Thus the hardened were taught to strike, endure, and strike again, until force itself became memory written into flesh and iron.
For power belongs not to the untouched, but to the one who survives the blow and returns it greater.
